questions.q: What does the Query Store baseline show for dbo.usp_CustomerOrderHistory?
options: ~15 ms / 640 logical reads for a consumer account vs. ~28 seconds / ~118,000 logical reads for a wholesale account like TrailWorks Co-op
The procedure performs identically for every customer regardless of order count
The procedure has never executed successfully in Query Store history
Duration is unrelated to which CustomerID is passed in
questions.explain: The baseline shows the same procedure costing roughly 190x more for a high-volume wholesale account than for a typical consumer account.

questions.q: What operator dominates the actual execution plan for the slow case, and why does it appear?
options: A Key Lookup against the clustered index, because IX_Orders_CustomerID doesn't carry OrderDate, OrderStatus, OrderTotal, or ShipDate
A Hash Match, because the query joins two large tables
A Table Scan, because there is no index on CustomerID at all
A Sort, because the ORDER BY is on an unindexed column
questions.explain: IX_Orders_CustomerID is non-covering — it seeks on CustomerID efficiently but triggers a Key Lookup per row for every other column the query needs.

questions.q: For TrailWorks Co-op's execution, roughly how many times does the Key Lookup operator run, and what share of the plan's cost does it represent?
options: About 18,400 times — over 90% of the plan's cost
Exactly once, with negligible cost
About 40 times, matching a typical consumer account
It doesn't appear in the plan at all
questions.explain: The Key Lookup runs once per qualifying row — about 18,400 times for this wholesale account — dominating the plan's cost.

questions.q: Which wait type dominates during the 10 AM-2 PM window when this query runs, and what does it indicate?
options: PAGEIOLATCH_SH — waits for shared latches while reading data pages from disk into the buffer pool, consistent with thousands of scattered Key Lookups
CXPACKET — indicating a parallelism skew problem unrelated to the plan
LCK_M_X — indicating a blocking lock problem on the Orders table
SOS_SCHEDULER_YIELD — indicating pure CPU pressure with no I/O involved
questions.explain: PAGEIOLATCH_SH waits confirm the plan's story: many Key Lookups against pages of a 14-million-row table that aren't all cached.

questions.q: How would you state the specific, named bottleneck this lesson identifies?
options: IX_Orders_CustomerID is a non-covering index for this query, so its cost scales linearly with a customer's order count
The MeridianRetail database server has run out of disk space
The stored procedure contains a T-SQL syntax error
The Orders table is missing its clustered index entirely
questions.explain: The plan and wait stats together point to one specific, actionable cause — a missing covering index — rather than a vague 'database is slow.'
